subject: Acid in its element, concept A (the acid spring at Dallol) against concept B (acid rain over wet black lava)
prompt: critic/ab/PROMPT-DUEL.txt, its second paragraph worded for two candidate pictures of the same page

judges.notes: Prefers B: wet volcanic rock and rain-dimpled water read as photographed at 1x and 3x; the gold cabinet (~129) glows against dark wet ground (~60); backlit overcast with a bright horizon band and a rippled gold reflection leading to the product; feet stand at the water's edge; crisp internals. A: the sulphur crust is smeared procedural displacement; the amber cabinet sits on crust of the same luma (~160) and dissolves; a milky grey sky fills ~40%; the chimney is a clay-like blob. B against: an olive/khaki grade (sky ~r176 g172 b144) makes the acrylic mustard; rain streaks over the horn read as scratches at 3x; centred, so a spread's gutter runs through the woofer; repeated splash crowns.

Prefers A: the three-quarter camera shows the box's depth, side panel and the horn's rear driver; the saturated amber horn keeps a crisp edge against a blue-grey sky; a low warm key from the left gives the box shape and a consistent shadow; a cleaner amber-and-teal palette. B: the square-on view flattens the product; the horn washes cream on cream against the pale sky; bone dry in a downpour; splash crowns read as CG sprites; the olive grade makes the amber brassy. A against: amber on amber-yellow sulphur so the base blends in; the crust is procedural noise at 3x; the chimney a clay-like blob; the amber out of gamut (blue <= 2 in ~46% of product pixels).

Prefers B: wet volcanic ground reads as real rock and mud; low-key backlight (p5-p95 ~38-214) separates the glowing cabinet from dark ground; feet stand in the puddle with a crisp amber reflection; cloud deck, horizon band and rain-hazed hills give weather and depth; smooth horn flare; the woofer's cap and surround read. A: the crust a game-engine heightmap at 3x; hazy and flat (~92-185) with the amber cabinet on same-yellow ground; blue clipped in ~55% of cabinet pixels so the panels posterise; little contact shadow; ruler-straight sprite-like steam. B against: the olive grade turns the acrylic khaki; the near-frontal view hides the driver; no droplets or wet sheen on the product in heavy rain; repeated splash sprites.

agreed: All three faulted A's sulphur crust (procedural noise at 3x) and its amber cabinet lost against same-coloured ground, and B's olive grade, its dry product in the rain and its CG splash crowns; two of three found B's straight-on view flat.
